# Generated files — the contract

> Landed here from a `⚙ GENERATED BY GITFACTORY` header? That file is compiler output. Edit the blueprint it names, regenerate, commit both. Never hand-edit it (golden rule #2).

This page is the one place that says which files in this repo the **compiler** writes, how to tell, how to regenerate them, and what guarantees (determinism, action pinning) the output carries. Every claim below is checked against `app/src/compiler/compile.ts` and the scripts in `app/scripts/`; when you change one of those, change this page in the same PR.

## What is generated, from what, by what

| Generated path | Source of truth | Regenerate with (from `app/`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/factory--gitorio-factory-{1,2,3}.yml` | `.factory/blueprint.json` (+ prompts in `.factory/prompts/`) | `compile()` over the blueprint — the app's **Deploy** button, or a one-off `vite-node` script that calls `compile(bp, { blueprintPath: '.factory/blueprint.json' })` and writes each `{ filename, yaml }` |
| `.github/workflows/factory--docs-gardener.yml`, `.factory/docs-gardener.blueprint.json`, `.factory/config.yml` | the `docs-gardener` gallery template in `app/src/templates/catalog.ts` + `app/src/content/model.ts` | `npx vite-node scripts/gen-docs-gardener.ts` |
| `examples/compiled/factory--*.yml` (the golden anchors) | `examples/*.blueprint.json` | `npx vite-node scripts/regen-examples.ts` — owns the directory: stale files are removed |
| `app/dist/` | the app source | `npm run build` — a build artifact, not committed |

Everything else in `.github/workflows/` (`ci.yml`, `deploy-pages.yml`, `claude.yml`, `evolve.yml`, `markdown-oneline.yml`) is hand-written: only files named `factory--<slug>.yml` are compiler output. `.factory/` is **source** (blueprints, prompts, `config.yml`), not output — the one exception being the docs-gardener trio above, which a script materialises from the template so the committed dogfood can never drift from the gallery.

### The map manifest

`app/public/maps/manifest.json` is written by the same `npm run maps` run, beside the maps: one entry per delivered map (`slug`, `type`, `source`, `hash`), sorted by slug so the file is byte-stable, and covered by `npm run maps:check` like every other file in that directory. The app imports it at build time (`app/src/map/manifest.ts`) to decide where an "Open delivered map" link or a Docs `::map <slug>` figure may point; a slug that is not listed renders a note, never a broken frame. Edit a blueprint or a demo fixture and regenerate — never the manifest.

## How to recognise a generated file

Every compiled workflow starts with exactly this two-line header (inline in `compile()`, `compile.ts`):

```yaml
# ⚙ GENERATED BY GITFACTORY — edit the blueprint, not this file.
# blueprint: .factory/blueprint.json  hash: 038bb273
```

The path is whatever `blueprintPath` the caller passed (default `.factory/blueprint.json`). The hash is `blueprintHash(bp)` in `app/src/blueprint/types.ts`: a 32-bit FNV-1a over `JSON.stringify({ nodes, edges, meta })`, rendered as 8 lowercase hex digits. It fingerprints the blueprint, not the YAML, so:

- header hash ≠ hash of the blueprint next to it → the blueprint moved and nobody regenerated (or someone hand-edited the YAML);
- the **Deploy** planner (`app/src/github/deploy.ts`) reads this header from the target repo and shows the *drift banner* when it disagrees with the blueprint it is about to deploy — a missing or garbled header counts as drifted.

Prompts (`.factory/prompts/*.md`) are deliberately **not** hashed: they are read by the agent at run time, so editing one is a hot change that needs no recompile (ARCHITECTURE § prompts).

## Determinism

`compile()` is a pure function of the blueprint plus explicit `CompileOptions` (`blueprintPath`, `pinActions`) — no I/O, no clock, no environment reads (golden rule #3). Compiling the same blueprint twice yields identical bytes; `regen-examples.ts` is idempotent for that reason, and `examples/compiled/` is the committed proof. If you ever want a timestamp, run id, hostname, or absolute path in generated output: don't — it belongs in `git log`, and it would break the reference-output tests.

## Action pinning

Compiled workflows reference exactly the third-party actions in the exported `PINNED_ACTIONS` table in `compile.ts` (`actions/checkout`, `anthropics/claude-code-action`, `dependabot/fetch-metadata`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `actions/download-artifact`, `peter-evans/create-pull-request`). Two modes:

- **Default** — floating major tags (`actions/checkout@v7`). Chosen so factories deployed into repos that keep tags by convention (law-ai) don't fight the target's style.
- **`meta.pinActions: true`** on the blueprint (or the `pinActions` compile option, ADR-026) — every emitted `uses:` becomes `owner/action@<40-char sha> # <tag>`, the tag restored as a trailing comment in a deterministic post-stringify pass.

Bumping a version is therefore a **compiler change**, never an edit to a `factory--*.yml`: Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem will keep opening PRs against the generated files (it did — #3, #55), and each one is reverted by the next regen. The procedure is: resolve the new tag (`git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> refs/tags/<tag>`, or `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>` — dereference annotated tags via `/git/tags/<sha>`), update the ref *and* the SHA in `PINNED_ACTIONS`, note the verification date in the comment above the table, regenerate everything in the table at the top of this page, and let the invariant tests confirm it. There is no separate "pin-check" CI job; the guard is the pinned-actions test in `compile.test.ts`, which fails if a `pinRef()` call site's ref is missing from the table or a bare `uses:` literal bypasses the wrapper. Re-verifying the table against live upstream refs from `/compile-check` is BL-20260818-02.

## Reviewing a PR that touches generated files

- A `factory--*.yml` diff with no blueprint / template / compiler diff is a hand edit — ask where it came from, then bounce it to the source.
- A blueprint or compiler diff with no regenerated output means the change isn't live yet; regenerate in the same PR.
- Review the blueprint for intent and the YAML for fidelity; the compiler invariant tests (`cd app && npm test`) plus `/compile-check` do the byte-level comparison.
